title: Define fallback semantics for model-version pinning during multi-region/tier rollouts
creator: Amit Patel
description:
Problem: When customers pin traffic to a specific model version while also using region/tier routing policies and applying canary or A/B rollouts, it's unclear how fallback should behave when the pinned variant is unavailable in the chosen region/tier or when capacity constraints force a downgrade. This leads to surprising errors (503s) or silent degradation (falling back to older model with different tokenization).

Goal: Define explicit, deterministic semantics for routing interactions between model-version pinning and rollout policies, update the router and policy engine, and provide observability so PMs and SREs can reason about user-visible degradation and SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: A clear spec describing order of evaluation between: explicit pin -> region selection -> tier routing -> rollout assignment -> fallback to compatible variant

Router implements the spec and passes integration tests for four scenarios (pinned present, pinned absent but variant available in region, pinned available but tier saturated, pinned unavailable globally)
Console exposes per-request attribution explaining why a non-pinned model was served (reason: region-mismatch, tier-capacity, rollout-fraction), with link to rollout config
No regression in tail latency or 95th percentile under standard simulation workload compared to baseline
Documentation updated (confluence + runtime docs) with examples and migration guidance
implementation_notes: Introduce routing decision tree in matcher: evaluate pin first; if pinned model artifact is reachable in policy-selected region and tier then route; otherwise consult fallback rules (explicit preferred fallback variants list, then compatible-models set, then best-effort region-tier routing)
Add model-availability-cache that tracks {model-version: [regions/tier-capacity-memo]} refreshed every 10s to avoid repeated global lookups
Add telemetry tags to request-span: pinned_model, resolved_model, fallback_reason (none | region-unavailable | tier-saturated | variant-incompatible | rollout-forced), resolved_region, resolved_tier

Implement a configuration knob per-tenant: pin_strictness = strict | prefer | best-effort (default prefer). strict -> fail fast if pin not available; prefer -> fallback to variant with audit; best-effort -> ignore pin and route for latency/cost reasons
Update policy UI to show pin_strictness and recommended settings for enterprise/Dedicated customers
architecture_decision: We choose a hybrid approach: evaluate explicit customer pin first but allow a per-tenant override (pin_strictness). This balances correctness (enterprise contracts that require exact model versions) with availability (hosted customers who prefer best-effort). We avoid silent implicit mapping of pinned version to newest compatible variant unless tenant is configured to allow it.
rollout_plan: Feature branch + unit tests: router/policy-engine changes behind feature flag
Stage on staging with canary traffic (10%) using synthetic workloads that exercise multi-region/tier splits
Enable observability hooks and dashboard before rolling to production
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with manual stop conditions on increase in error budget consumption
Post-rollout retrospective and update docs/SDK examples
test_plan: Unit tests for decision tree permutations (pin present/absent x region available/unavailable x tier saturated/not)
Integration tests using local multi-region simulator that toggles availability and capacity
Chaos test: simulate region outage and verify strict pins return defined error and prefer pins fallback with telemetry recorded
Load test with tail-latency measurement comparing baseline and new router under synthetic mix (LLM chat + embeddings)
qa_checks: All integration tests green in CI
Feature flag gating verified in prod-staging
Console exposition shows fallback_reason for 100 recent requests
No customer-facing 5xx increase for customers in rollout cohort
